subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music For Sociocultural And Political Expression
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a Classical concerto first movement, the cadenza traditionally occurs at which point?
options: Near the end, over a tonic six-four before the final tutti
In the middle of the development only
At the very opening before the orchestra plays
questions.explain: The cadenza, a virtuosic solo passage, typically falls near the movement's end on a cadential six-four leading to the closing tutti.

questions.q: In music production, 'multitracking' refers to...?
options: Compressing a stereo mix into mono
Recording different parts onto separate tracks so they can be balanced and edited independently
Playing many instruments live in one take with no overdubs
questions.explain: Multitracking records parts on separate tracks, allowing independent editing and mixing.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the Brandenburg Concertos?
questions.explain: J. S. Bach composed the six Brandenburg Concertos, exemplars of the late Baroque concerto.

questions.q: In fusion music, an artist such as Ravi Shankar collaborating with Western musicians most exemplifies...?
options: The blending of Indian classical techniques (raga, tala, sitar) with Western elements
questions.explain: Such collaborations blend Indian classical features like raga, tala and sitar with Western musical elements.

questions.q: In song structure terminology, a 'bridge' (or 'middle eight') typically functions to...?
options: End the song with a fade-out
Provide contrast in melody/harmony before returning to the chorus or verse
State the main hook for the first time
questions.explain: The bridge offers contrasting material that breaks up verse-chorus repetition before a return.

questions.q: In jazz performance, 'swung' quavers are most accurately understood as pairs of quavers played roughly as...?
options: A short-long anticipation on every beat
A triplet feel, long-short (approximately quarter-eighth of a triplet)
questions.explain: Swung quavers approximate a triplet division, giving a long-short 'lilt' to each pair.

questions.q: Neoclassicism in the 20th century is characterised by which approach?
options: Reviving Classical and Baroque forms with modern harmony
questions.explain: Neoclassicism, associated with Stravinsky, revisits older forms and clarity while applying a modern harmonic language.

questions.q: The concerto grosso typically contrasts which two performing groups?
questions.explain: The Baroque concerto grosso opposes a small group of soloists (concertino) against the full ensemble (ripieno or tutti).

questions.q: The 32-bar 'AABA' song form, common in jazz standards, consists of...?
options: A twelve-bar blues repeated until the soloist stops
Four eight-bar sections where the third (B) provides a contrasting 'bridge'
questions.explain: AABA form has four eight-bar sections, with the B section serving as a contrasting bridge.

questions.q: Swing-era big bands such as Count Basie's typically organised their players into which sectional layout?
questions.explain: Big bands are built around a saxophone section, a brass section and a rhythm section.

questions.q: A Neapolitan sixth chord is a major triad built on which scale degree, usually in first inversion?
questions.explain: The Neapolitan sixth is a major triad on the flattened supertonic (flattened second degree), typically used in first inversion.

questions.q: In a 'verse-chorus' pop structure, a 'pre-chorus' serves to...?
options: Build anticipation and lead smoothly from the verse into the chorus
questions.explain: The pre-chorus builds momentum and links the verse to the chorus.

questions.q: A 'walking bass' line in jazz is most characterised by which feature?
options: A sustained pedal note held under the harmony
A steady stream of crotchets outlining the chords, usually one note per beat
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in even crotchets, typically one note per beat, threading through the chord tones to drive the harmony forward.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'father of the symphony' and the 'father of the string quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive output shaped both the Classical symphony and the string quartet.

questions.q: A fugue opens with which compositional procedure?
options: A subject stated alone then imitated by successive voices
questions.explain: A fugue begins with a subject announced in one voice, answered imitatively by entering voices.

questions.q: A 'cyclic' or 'ostinato' pattern, common in African drumming, is...?
options: A pattern that constantly changes and never repeats
A short rhythmic or melodic pattern repeated continuously as a foundation
questions.explain: Cyclic patterns repeat a short rhythmic or melodic cell continuously, forming the music's foundation.

questions.q: In Celtic folk music, a 'jig' is most commonly in which metre?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance typically in compound 6/8 time.

questions.q: A tonic pedal is best described as which device?
options: A sustained tonic note held while harmonies change above it
A modulation to the tonic minor
A rapid alternation of tonic and dominant
A melodic ornament on the tonic
questions.explain: A pedal is a sustained or repeated note, the tonic pedal holding the tonic while other parts move through changing harmonies.

questions.q: Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons' is an example of which Baroque genre?
questions.explain: 'The Four Seasons' consists of four solo violin concertos, a leading Baroque solo-concerto example.

questions.q: Motown, the Detroit-based label of the 1960s, is associated with which of the following hallmarks?
options: Free improvisation with no fixed form
A polished soul-pop sound with the 'Funk Brothers' house band, tambourine back-beats and call-and-response vocals
questions.explain: Motown produced a slick soul-pop sound built on a house band, back-beat percussion and gospel-derived call-and-response vocals.

questions.q: Ragtime, popularised by Scott Joplin, is principally characterised by which rhythmic device?
options: Rubato throughout with no fixed pulse
A swung shuffle feel in the bass
A syncopated, off-beat melody set against a steady march-like bass
Continuous polyrhythmic layering of three rhythms
questions.explain: Ragtime sets a syncopated right-hand melody against a regular, march-style stride bass.

questions.q: In African drumming traditions, the West African 'djembe' is...?
options: A set of tuned metal gongs
questions.explain: The djembe is a goblet-shaped West African hand drum capable of a wide range of tones.

questions.q: An Alberti bass is which kind of accompaniment figure?
options: A broken-chord pattern in the left hand of keyboard music
questions.explain: The Alberti bass breaks a chord into a steady low-high-middle-high arpeggiated pattern, common in the Classical era.

questions.q: The effect known as 'delay' produces which result?
options: One or more distinct repeats (echoes) of the original signal
A panning of sound between left and right speakers
A widening of the stereo field by phase inversion
questions.explain: Delay creates discrete repeats, or echoes, of the original sound.

questions.q: The compositional device of 'augmentation' refers to...?
options: Raising the pitch of a theme
Lengthening the note values of a theme, usually doubling them
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens a theme's note values, typically doubling each duration.

questions.q: A 4-3 suspension resolves by which means?
options: The third rises to the fourth
The fourth steps down to the third
The fourth leaps up to the sixth
questions.explain: In a 4-3 suspension the dissonant fourth resolves downwards by step onto the consonant third.

questions.q: The technique of word-painting describes which practice?
options: Music that reflects the literal meaning of the text
Painting visual scenery for an opera
questions.explain: Word-painting depicts the meaning of the words in the music, such as rising lines on the word 'ascend'.

questions.q: In the context of performance, 'idiomatic writing' for an instrument means...?
options: Writing that ignores the instrument's natural strengths
Writing only in the treble clef
Writing that suits the technique, range and characteristic capabilities of the instrument
questions.explain: Idiomatic writing exploits the natural technique, range and strengths of the specific instrument.

questions.q: The standard Classical string quartet comprises which instruments?
options: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
questions.explain: A string quartet is scored for two violins, one viola and one cello.

questions.q: Brahms is generally regarded as a Romantic composer who upheld which trait?
options: Classical formal structures within a Romantic idiom
questions.explain: Brahms combined Romantic expression with Classical forms such as the symphony and sonata, in the absolute-music tradition.
